title: Analytical results for the Shannon entropy of the critical transverse-field Ising chain
abstract: Local-basis Shannon entropies of critical wave functions contain universal subleading information, but the Shannon point of the critical transverse-field Ising chain is singular in the conventional Rényi approach. We treat it directly at $n=1$ by representing the complete computational-basis Born distribution as the odd-degree boundary of independent long-range Bernoulli edges. The Shannon chain rule separates the entropy into explicit independent-edge and conditional cycle-space terms. For the periodic chain this isolates the analytic edge anomaly and organizes the remaining constant by linked vertex support. Conditional on the stated finite-part matching and forest assumptions, every nonvanishing linked coefficient is represented by an explicit finite-dimensional integral, giving an all-orders analytic hierarchy; the four-vertex term is evaluated in closed form, and the first few linked sectors already nearly saturate the established periodic constant, which is also reconstructed independently from the exact finite-size distribution. For an interval, the exterior reduces exactly to one ghost vertex and the explicit squared logarithms cancel, leaving the analytic edge contribution $γ_E=\log2/4-1/16$. The conditional cycle term has an exact all-support decomposition into physical-line and ghost-linked sectors; conditional on closure of the boundary forest subtraction, these sectors define an all-orders hierarchy of renormalized line and monomer--dimer boundary periods for the remaining logarithmic coefficient. The first complete augmented linked coefficient is evaluated in closed form, with an exact cancellation between its line and ghost boundary-layer anomalies; an independent reconstruction from exact finite-size probabilities recovers the established coefficient $γ_1=0.060020(3)$.
summary: This theoretical paper calculates the Shannon entropy for the critical transverse-field Ising chain by treating the problem directly at the singular point $n=1$. It employs advanced techniques involving graph theory and the Shannon chain rule to decompose the entropy into manageable, analytically solvable components. The work successfully derives universal constants characterizing the system's critical behavior, confirming previous results through a novel, rigorous mathematical framework.
main_problem: The paper determines the Shannon entropy of the critical transverse-field Ising (TFI) chain, specifically addressing the singularity encountered when using the conventional Rényi approach at the Shannon point ($n=1$).
main_result: The entropy is decomposed into explicit independent-edge and conditional cycle-space terms, yielding an all-orders analytic hierarchy and recovering established universal coefficients like $\gamma_1$ and $\gamma_E$ through rigorous mathematical techniques.
method: The analysis uses the Shannon chain rule applied to the Born distribution, representing it via independent long-range Bernoulli edges and analyzing the resulting graph cycle space structure.
model_or_system: The system is the critical transverse-field Ising (TFI) chain, analyzed using its ground-state probability distribution derived from the Hamiltonian. The mathematical framework involves mapping the probability distribution to a boundary problem on a graph.
key_observables: Shannon entropy ($H_1$), analytic edge anomaly ($\gamma_E$), and the universal logarithmic coefficient ($\gamma_1$).
important_parameters: The critical point of the TFI chain, the finite size $L$, and the Shannon index $n=1$.
main_assumptions: The results are conditional on stated finite-part matching and forest assumptions, and the analysis relies on controlling residual information in the graph cycle space.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by establishing the entropy decomposition via the Shannon chain rule, evaluating specific terms (like the four-vertex term), and then deriving the final universal constants ($\gamma_E$ and $\gamma_1$) by analyzing the boundary and cycle-space contributions.
why_interesting: The rigorous mathematical treatment of entanglement and information measures (Shannon entropy) at quantum critical points provides deep insights into the universal scaling laws governing quantum many-body systems, which is crucial for understanding quantum phase transitions.
